<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**7** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7d061681a67d72467af14b318fc47aed234bf23a` — the merge of head `4fd21ab554239916207b89bfc43686e2b7dc5fe7` into base `3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7d061681a67d72467af14b318fc47aed234bf23a && git checkout 7d061681a67d72467af14b318fc47aed234bf23a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6 4fd21ab554239916207b89bfc43686e2b7dc5fe7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6 && git merge --no-ff 4fd21ab554239916207b89bfc43686e2b7dc5fe7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-17T11:14Z

Head-sha: ae5008bed7a29ec230a079dd143de537da9f3be3
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c (thread "Review seat 3 L1-c"), for card #34686 PR1 (claim 6944687739, dev report 6945837392).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Part of #34686.`; no closing keyword anywhere in the body next to any issue number (#34685, #34761, #34763 are named with no verb). Part of is right: the card's second acceptance item (the `/mcp/skill` pin test) is PR2's, behind #34685.

**Scope vs claim.** Six files, all inside PR1's claimed surface: `packages/mcp/src/**` (3 files), `packages/mcp/README.md`, `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`, root `.changeset/`. No `skills/**`, no `packages/runtime/**`, no `content/docs/releases/`. Not re-exported from `packages/mcp/src/index.ts` (diff touches no index), so the two new functions add no public export.

**Governed / size.** `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34790` (run at origin/main f02f4f63): `0 of 6 path(s) hit the register … NOT governed`, `391 changed line(s) ≤ 3000`. No Tier H. Seat's face call (no L2) stands: no spec, schema or wire-shape file moved.

**Changeset.** `@objectstack/mcp` (published, `18.5.0`, no `private`) is the only package whose `src/**` moved, and it is named. Level `patch` matches `Metadata-protocol: none`. `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` match the claim and the PR body.

**Check-runs at ae5008be.** 57 runs, every one `success` or `skipped`; `Lint & Repo Gates` success, `TypeScript Type Check` success, `Test Core` and all 8 shards success, `Check Changeset` success, `PR-body guards` success, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success, `Build Docs` and `Check Documentation Links` success.

**Tests.** Real commands with output in the body (package typecheck + test-layer ledger unchanged; whole `@objectstack/mcp` suite 67 files / 1233 tests; new file 7 tests). The new file asserts each branch against its own `tools/list` control, so the rule's gate and the registration gate are pinned together. Two ablations through `ablation-replace.mjs`, each red on the right test and restored to the HEAD blob. Not re-run here (no install in this container); CI `Test Core` on this head covers the package.

**Card acceptance.**
1. Fresh `initialize` on `examples/app-crm` returns the rule and the install line (admin key, 812 B, dataset pair listed) and neither dataset sentence for a grant without `data:read` (`data:write` token, 357 B, 4 tools). Met, live readings in the body.
2. `/mcp/skill` pin test: PR2. Not owed here (Part of).
3. Byte count stated: 98 → 812 / 357. Met.
4. "The four documents mention the dataset tools": README and connect-mcp here; the two `skills/**` mentions moved to #34685 per the claim. Met for this half.

**Prose read against the diff (the seat's ask), sentence by sentence.**
- README "first of: the host's per-request text (`instructions` / `dataOnlyInstructions` on the authoring injection), the `instructions` option, or the open server's own text" = `hostInstructions(...) ?? this.config.instructions ?? openServerInstructions(...)`; `hostInstructions` picks `instructions` vs `dataOnlyInstructions` by `grantsAuthoringTools` and returns the text unmodified (blank = absent). True.
- README / connect-mcp "only where this request registers both `list_datasets` and `query_dataset`" = `datasetToolsServed` → `datasetToolDescriptions`, the same function `registerDatasetTools` now registers from. True.
- README "only when it implements all three of `listDatasets`, `queryDataset` and `datasetToolDefinitions`" = `hasDatasetTools`. "the runtime's bridge does where the analytics service serves its dataset executor" = `resolveMcpDatasetToolsService` / `buildMcpBridge` seam (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts:243-244, 1451-1452, 1477-1486`). True.
- README `data:read` "covers … and the dataset pair"; connect-mcp "A token without `data:read` gets neither tool" = the scope check moved verbatim into `datasetToolDescriptions` (unscoped grant keeps the pair). True.
- "at this package's own version (the two are released together)" = `PACKAGE_VERSION`; `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/skills` are both in the one `fixed` group of `.changeset/config.json`, both at 18.5.0. True.
- connect-mcp tool rows: `list_datasets` "which of the question's words each one matches exactly" = `matches` in `LIST_DATASETS_DESCRIPTION` (service-analytics `dataset-tools.ts:85-96`); `query_dataset` "the answer carries its provenance" = `QUERY_DATASET_DESCRIPTION` + `DatasetProvenanceSchema`. True.
- connect-mcp link `/docs/ai/skills` exists and its install section says the sync step the install line points to ("follow the package README to sync") — `packages/skills/README.md:23-50` has it. True.
- README / connect-mcp "stdio … carry neither part" and "the `instructions` option serves that text as written instead" = the stdio constructor path is untouched and the configured branch precedes the open-server text. True.
- The rule text itself condenses ADR-0149 D3 rules 1-4 (exact name/label/synonym hit; one measure hit → `query_dataset`; several → ask, never pick; none → `query_records` / `aggregate_records`, labelled) and says nothing D3 does not. True.
- Grepped `content/docs/**` (excluding generated references), `skills/**` and `packages/spec/src/ai/**` for any sentence describing the `initialize` instructions as one sentence or as the default text: none, so nothing else is made false.
- Changeset sentences match the code paths above.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1. The instructions rule leaves out two D3 parts the tool descriptions still carry: render the source from `provenance` (rule 2) and "a dimension hit alone is not an answer" (rule 5). "One measure match" covers rule 5 by wording; provenance is read once the client is inside `query_dataset`. Fine for a "few lines" text; if PR2's single-source skill makes the served text the reference, a later pin could compare this rule against it.
- N2. Out-of-scope findings (configured `instructions` option and stdio carry neither part) are recorded in the body as noted, not filed; the epic seat decides whether the option contract gets a card.
- N3. The dev report says the body ends with a plain-text signed line; the body at this head ends with the `<!-- signed: … -->` comment the dispatch relay parses, which is what standard-order asks. No action.

Landing: o3-E lands on this ACCEPT (non-governed). A later push owes an L1-c delta read.
